newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia presents draft privatisation law.
newsitem.headline: Serbia presents draft privatisation law.

text.p: Serbian government presented on Monday its new draft privatisation law rejecting mass privatisation but envisaging heavy discounts for employees, pensioners and other investors.
Privatisation will not be compulsory but legislators said the size of offered discounts will stimulate the process.
Technically, after one month of fine-tuning the draft, the final version will be submitted to the parliament with privatisation expected to begin in July.

"This year has been rightfully announced as a reform year because reforms are an important precondition for the restructuring of the Serbian economy and its integration with international economy and finance," Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic said.
"We see ownership transformation and privatisation as part of the entire reform process," he said.
Marjanovic said the law is based on efficiency, fairness and transparency and will be highly stimulating.
Serbian Minister of Privatisation Milan Beko said the law changes the ownership structure of the Serbian economy and is the most important legal document of the state.
Beko promised the government will inform the public on the privatisation process via all media.
The law will be accompanied by other projects such as repayment of all hard-currency savings and rehabilitation of the banking system.
The first stage of privatisation will last three years.
The law also envisages three forms of selling the socially-owned capital: sell-off with discounts, capitalisation issues and debt-for-equity swap.

Privatisation receipts will be directed to three state funds: 50 percent to the Serbian development funds and 25 percent to the Serbian pension fund and Serbian labour market office each. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
